abstract: We develop a projection-based decomposition to disentangle structural breaks in the factor variance and factor loadings. Our approach yields test statistics that can be compared against standard distributions commonly used in the structural break literature. Because standard methods for estimating factor models in macroeconomics normalize the factor variance, they do not distinguish between breaks of the factor variance and factor loadings. Applying our procedure to U.S. macroeconomic data, we find that the Great Moderation is more naturally accommodated as a break in the factor variance as opposed to a break in the factor loadings, in contrast to extant procedures which do not tell the two apart and thus interpret the Great Moderation as a structural break in the factor loadings. Through our projection-based decomposition, we estimate that the Great Moderation is associated with an over 70% reduction in the total factor variance, highlighting the relevance of disentangling breaks in the factor structure.
title: Disentangling Structural Breaks in Factor Models for Macroeconomic Data

abstract: Regularization methods are crucial for the analysis of high-dimensional data, with most methods adding a penalty term to the loss function explicitly. In this paper, we introduce an implicit regularization technique through over-parameterization and propose a calibrated penalty-free (CPF) estimation method for high-dimensional linear errors-in-variables models. This method calibrates the bias caused by measurement errors while avoiding the bias introduced by penalty terms. We use the gradient descent algorithm to minimize the over-parameterized calibrated loss function without penalties, resulting in a sparse estimate of regression coefficients and thus achieving implicit regularization. Furthermore, a novel bootstrap methodology is introduced to address the challenge posed by the unknown covariance matrix of measurement errors. The oracle inequality for estimation error is established under certain regularity conditions. Extensive simulation studies and a real data analysis illustrate the competitive finite sample performance of the proposed method.
title: From Penalization to Over-Parameterization: Achieving Implicit Regularization for High-Dimensional Linear Errors-in-Variables Models

abstract: Models of electoral accountability typically assume a politician provides a public good. Yet in many contexts, elected officials distribute private goods among voters with conflicting interests. We present a formal model to analyze this situation. An elected official allocates a rivalrous good to a number of voters, who each observe their own allocation but neither others’ allocations nor the official’s action. Each voter’s challenge is to determine whether the incumbent stole from other voters when deciding to sack or retain the incumbent. This problem can be resolved if voters retain the incumbent probabilistically, so that the vote of any voter from whom the incumbent steals is effectively up-weighted. However, this benefit of probabilistic voting also comes with a cost, since the fact that the incumbent may be sacked by mistake diminishes the allocation they are willing to provide to voters.
abstract_zh: 选举问责模型通常假设政治家提供公共产品。然而在许多情境中，民选官员会在利益冲突的选民之间分配私人产品。我们构建了一个正式模型来分析这种情况。一位民选官员将竞争性物品分配给若干选民，每位选民仅能观察到自身所得分配，既无法获知他人分配情况，也无法了解官员的具体行为。当决定是否罢免现任官员时，每位选民面临的挑战在于判断该官员是否侵占了其他选民的应得利益。若选民以概率化方式决定是否留任现任官员，这一问题便可得到解决——因为当官员侵占某位选民利益时，该选民的投票权重实际上会被提升。然而，这种概率化投票机制也伴随着代价：由于官员可能因误判而被罢免，这会降低其愿意向选民提供的分配额度。
title: Electoral accountability, distributive conflict, and probabilistic voting
title_zh: 选举问责、分配冲突与概率投票

abstract: This paper empirically confronts two different channels driving the 2000s boom‐bust and the recent strong appreciation of house prices in Europe. The first channel, the fundamental view, is characterized by income and credit. While the expectational view is based on the expectations of households and construction firms. I propose a Panel Factor Augmented Vector Autoregressive (FAVAR) model that can determine these views' importance. First, the results show that expectations play a significant role in short‐ and medium‐run fluctuations of house prices, explaining 30% and 20%, respectively. Second, the effect of a household's belief shock on house prices depends on the level of mortgage credit liberalization. Specifically, in countries with looser credit conditions, household beliefs significantly impact house prices. While in countries with tighter credit conditions, the impact is not significant. Overall, this research provides new evidence that credit market conditions can influence the effect of expectations on house prices.
abstract_zh: 本文通过实证分析，对比了推动2000年代房地产繁荣与衰退以及近期欧洲房价强劲上涨的两种不同机制。第一种机制，即基本面观点，以收入和信贷为特征；而预期观点则基于家庭和建筑企业的预期。我提出了一种面板因子增强向量自回归（FAVAR）模型，用以确定这两种观点的重要性。首先，结果显示，预期在房价的短期和中长期波动中扮演重要角色，分别解释了30%和20%的波动。其次，家庭信念冲击对房价的影响取决于抵押贷款信贷自由化的程度。具体而言，在信贷条件较为宽松的国家，家庭信念对房价有显著影响；而在信贷条件较为严格的国家，这种影响则不显著。总体而言，本研究提供了新的证据，表明信贷市场条件能够影响预期对房价的作用。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Understanding the Drivers of Housing Prices: Fundamental versus Expectational View
title_zh: 理解房价驱动因素：基本面与预期视角

abstract: We develop a model with labor‐market matching frictions that is subject to a range of shocks, including shocks to matching efficiency and bargaining power, and use the model to examine how monetary policy should respond to such shocks. We show that optimal monetary policy responds effectively to these shocks, producing economic outcomes that are close to the flex‐price equilibrium. Moreover, this effectiveness remains if monetary policy is conducted with discretion, indicating that time inconsistency and forward guidance are not central to the policy response.
abstract_zh: 我们构建了一个包含劳动力市场匹配摩擦的模型，该模型受到一系列冲击的影响，包括匹配效率和议价能力的冲击，并利用该模型探讨货币政策应如何应对这些冲击。研究表明，最优货币政策能有效应对这些冲击，使经济结果接近弹性价格均衡。此外，即便在相机抉择的货币政策下，这种有效性依然存在，这表明时间不一致性和前瞻指引并非政策应对的核心要素。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: Policy Biases in a Model with Labor‐Market Frictions
title_zh: 劳动力市场摩擦模型中的政策偏向

abstract: We address how different restrictions or “strings” attached to the usage of government aid distributed through banks during crises affect subprime consumer debt. Leveraging quasi‐natural experiments, we compare Troubled Asset Relief Program (TARP), characterized by limits on executive and shareholder compensation but no strings attached to lending with the highly restrictive Paycheck Protection Program (PPP) loan requirements but no limits on executives and shareholders. We evaluate the programs’ impacts on millions of consumer debt observations from the Consumer Credit Panel. Results indicate that the PPP funds significantly reduced debt for subprime borrowers, primarily through income shock mechanisms, compared to additional debt through credit shocks under TARP.
abstract_zh: 我们探讨了危机期间通过银行分配的政府援助所附加的不同限制或“条件”如何影响次级消费债务。利用准自然实验，我们将问题资产救助计划（TARP）与高度限制性的薪资保护计划（PPP）贷款要求进行比较，前者以高管和股东薪酬限制为特征，但贷款无附加条件，后者则对高管和股东无限制。我们评估了这些计划对消费者信用面板中数百万条消费债务观测数据的影响。结果表明，与TARP下通过信贷冲击导致的额外债务相比，PPP资金主要通过收入冲击机制显著减少了次级借款人的债务。
journal: Journal of Money, Credit and Banking
title: A Tale of Two Bailouts and Their Impact on Subprime Consumer Debt
title_zh: 两轮救助计划及其对次级消费债务的影响
